entry.title: Nicolai Vitti — DPSCD Superintendent Who Authorized PCA
entry.content:
Position

FieldValue
NameNicolai Vitti, Ph.D.
TitleSuperintendent, Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD)
Relationship to BanksMentor — regular meetings on academic progress, legislation
RoleAuthorized Purpose Charter Academy under DPSCD oversight
Authorization dateJuly 2025
TCR 22-12Testified in support, wrote letter of recommendation

TCR 22-12 Testimony (February 9, 2023)

Vitti testified under oath and wrote a support letter. He described Banks as:

  • “Reflective, thoughtful, child-centric leader”
  • Having “skills, character, and integrity required of a Michigan school administrator”
  • Someone who “has taken responsibility for and learned from his past mistakes”

He planned to continue mentoring Banks after the certificate was issued.

What Happened Under His Watch

MetricValue
MacDowell math proficiencyBottom 3% statewide
Revenue extracted by Purpose Group$4,285,201 (72.67%)
PCA charter authorized byDPSCD (Vitti’s district)
PCA authorized despiteBanks’s 8 felony convictions
$348,489 unaccountedIn public financial statements

The Most Vulnerable Children

PCA was authorized to serve:

  • Homeless children
  • Chronically absent children
  • Children in the juvenile justice system

Projected enrollment: 225 students, growing to 400.

These are the children with the fewest alternatives. Homeless kids who need stability. Kids in juvenile detention who need a path out. Chronically absent kids whose lives are already chaos. They got a school run by a man with 8 felony convictions who lives with a convicted drug offender — while 72.67% of their education funding flows through a sole-member LLC.

DPSCD gets paid ~$81,000/year to authorize this arrangement.

The Mentorship Gap

Vitti described Banks as “child-centric.” The schools produce:

  • 3% math proficiency
  • 72.67% of revenue flowing to a private LLC
  • $348,489 unaccounted in public financial statements
  • Children educated by a man who told police “I am a lawyer”

DPSCD Authorization Pipeline

DPSCD’s board includes Misha Stallworth West — stepdaughter of Nicole Wells-Stallworth (MacDowell Board President, wife of Thomas Stallworth III). The charter authorization for Banks’s schools passes through a board that includes the superintendent’s patron’s family member.

Questions for Investigation

  1. Board vote — Who on the DPSCD board voted to authorize PCA? Was Misha Stallworth West on the board at that time? If she voted yes, the pipeline is complete: Wells-Stallworth hires Banks at MacDowell → stepdaughter Misha authorizes PCA
  2. Background check — Did DPSCD verify Banks’ criminal record before authorization? Michigan charter law requires it
  3. J.D. verification — Did DPSCD verify Banks’ claimed law degree? He lists a J.D. from MSU Law not confirmed by bar records
  4. Conflict of interest — Did any board member with a social or financial relationship to Banks participate in the authorization decision?
  5. Enrollment data — Has PCA reached projected enrollment? What are the outcomes for these vulnerable children?

Verify

  • DPSCD Superintendent: detroitk12.org
  • DPSCD board meeting minutes: July 2025 charter authorization vote
  • DPSCD charter authorization records for Purpose Charter Academy
  • Michigan charter school law: background check requirements for charter operators
  • DPSCD budget: authorization fee calculations
  • TCR 22-12 hearing transcript (MOAHR records)

All sources: TCR 22-12 Final Decision (Aug 4, 2023), MDE FOIA, DPSCD charter authorization records, public school performance data, and board meeting minutes.

entry.title: Four Dynasties — The Machine Behind the School
entry.content:
Four interlocking dynasties converge on one charter school enterprise. Each contributed a structural component that makes the machine run:

What Each Dynasty Contributed

DynastyStructural RoleFederal RecordWhat They Gave Banks
Banks/Flenory (BMF)Blood lineageOD Banks: BMF Defendant #22. Tonesa Welch: BMF defendantThe family brand. The extraction playbook. The zero-accountability narrative.
StallworthSocial incubationKeith: $20K gang money laundering (2003)BCF board access → family donations → MacDowell Board President → DPSCD authorization pipeline
SabreeJudicial captureFBI-probed 2019, Bowles class action2 children on the bench covering the enterprise’s courts. Foreclosure pipeline.
KilpatrickPolitical infrastructureKwame: 24 federal RICO feloniesPR machine (Dumas), dark money (Daniels → Detroit Leaders), charter authorization (Gay-Dagnogo), and the brand association (Carolyn at CBC party)

The Structuring Pattern — Two Decades, One Crime

WhoWhenAmountFor WhomMethodSentence
Keith Stallworth1998 (pled 2003)$20,000“A gang”False CTR at Michigan National Bank — hid true ownerPlea deal (conspiracy charges dropped)
Kenneth Daniels2010 (convicted 2014)$19,000Drug kingpin Carlos PowellTwo cashier’s checks at two banks — evaded $10K reporting1 year
Brian Banks2003–2016MultipleHimselfCheck fraud, forgery, financial transaction device, false pretenses≤8 months + 1 day total

Three men. Three structuring schemes. Three barely-there sentences. All three remained active in Detroit politics. All three connected to the same network.

The Powell drug operation that Daniels served: $21 million laundered, 12 kg cocaine, 30 kg heroin, 1,000 lbs marijuana. Both Powell brothers got life. Daniels got one year. Keith Stallworth’s conspiracy charges were dropped. Banks has served less than nine months total across 9 convictions.

The Racial Solidarity Shield

All four dynasties used the same armor: racial solidarity.

The Stallworths ran the Black Caucus Foundation. The Sabrees built a judicial dynasty in the most Black city in America. The Kilpatricks embodied Black political power in Detroit. Banks frames himself as a “redemption story” for a Black community that believes in second chances.

The armor works because it exploits something real. The history of racism against Black Detroiters is not fabricated. The distrust of institutions that have failed Black communities is earned. The desire for Black leadership in Black institutions is legitimate.

But when that legitimate desire is weaponized to protect a man who produces 3% math proficiency — when 97% of overwhelmingly Black children cannot do grade-level math while $4.9 million flows through shell entities — the armor is not protecting the community. It is trapping them inside the machine.

The crack trade destroyed these neighborhoods. The foreclosure pipeline stripped them of wealth. Kwame’s corruption bankrupted their city. And now the children who grew up in that wreckage sit in classrooms run by the same families, at the same addresses, with the same zero-accountability playbook — and they can’t do math.

The machine survived every prosecution. It survived the crack era, the RICO case, the FBI probes, the money laundering pleas. It put on a suit. It moved into the school system. It counts heads for per-pupil funding.

The Convergence Points

Where all four dynasties physically intersected:

VenueWho Was ThereWhat Happened
2023 CBC Party, Grand Hyatt DCBanks (host), Carolyn Cheeks Kilpatrick (honorary host), Nicole Wells-Stallworth (honoree)Party-to-board pipeline: honorees became board members
Black Caucus Foundation of MichiganBanks (board), Keith Stallworth (Managing Dir), Virgil Smith (board), Bert Johnson (board)Reunion of felons — where Banks met the Stallworths
MacDowell Prep, 4201 W Outer DrBanks (superintendent), Wells-Stallworth (Board President), Misha Stallworth West (DPSCD authorizer)Extraction point — $4.9M/yr, 3% math
Wayne County CourthouseJudges Sabree, Sabree, Yancey, Perkins, MillerJudicial capture — enterprise cases land before network judges
DPSCD BoardGay-Dagnogo (authorized PCA), Misha Stallworth West, Corletta VaughnCharter authorization pipeline
Michigan LegislatureBanks, Gay-Dagnogo, Keith Stallworth, Thomas Stallworth III, Kenneth Daniels, Bert JohnsonWhere the political relationships were forged
Banks’ book acknowledgmentsKaren Dumas, Sherry Gay-Dagnogo, Todd PerkinsBanks named them in his own published work

The Intermediaries — Where the Dynasties Meet the Schools

The dynasties provide the infrastructure. But someone has to physically connect the political power to the school operation. These intermediaries are the new family blood — not dynasty heirs, but operators who embedded themselves across multiple institutions in sequence, creating the handoff chains.

Judge Tenisha Yancey — The Bridge ✅ Verified 

JIMMY SETTLES (UAW Vice President)
    └── uncle of
TENISHA YANCEY
    ├── Worked at Wayne County Land Bank (Sabree's domain, 2007-2013)
    ├── Wayne County Exec Office (Evans)
    ├── Wayne County Prosecutor (juvenile)
    ├── Harper Woods Board of Ed (Banks' suburb)
    ├── Succeeded Banks in HD-1 (Nov 2017)
    ├── 36th District Judge (Nov 2022) — same court as Adam Sabree + Sean Perkins
    ├── MacDowell Board Chair
    ├── SOLE campaign activity: $383.82 to Banks' LLC
    ├── Paid son Jaylen $2,935 from campaign
    └── SISTER: Dr. Chalena Yancey Beasley → PCA School Leader

She sat in every institution in sequence: Sabree’s land bank → county government → prosecutor’s office → Banks’ suburban school board → Banks’ legislative seat → the bench → Banks’ school board. Each stop added a layer of institutional access. → Full Yancey Profile

Sherry Gay-Dagnogo — The Golden Parachute ✅ Verified 

GAY-DAGNOGO

    │   ├── Rallied for Banks at AG charges (2016)
    │   ├── Defended Banks' plea deal (2017)

She defended Banks publicly, authorized his school, paid his drug trafficker associate, then took a 10-year appointment running the office that handles complaints about the system she captured. → Full Gay-Dagnogo Profile

Bishop Corletta Vaughn — The Authorization Chair 📄 Documented

entry.title: Alma Stallworth — Dynasty Matriarch
entry.content:
Position

FieldValue
NameAlma G. Stallworth
OfficeMichigan House of Representatives — 21 years
FoundedBlack Caucus Foundation of Michigan (BCF)
BCF salary (2015)$18,000 (per IRS Form 990)

The Foundation She Built

Alma Stallworth served 21 years in the Michigan Legislature and founded the Black Caucus Foundation of Michigan. The BCF’s stated mission, per its 2015 federal tax return: “to decrease usage of drugs and alcohol among youth.”

The foundation she built became the institutional vehicle her son Keith used while managing a federal guilty plea for laundering money from illegal activities through a strip club. The same foundation incubated Brian Banks — a 9-time convicted felon who now runs two charter schools at 3% math proficiency.

Family

PersonRoleStatus
Keith StallworthSon — State Rep, Wayne Co. CommissionerFederal guilty plea (2003) — gang money laundering
Thomas Stallworth IIISon — State Rep (2011-2015)Director, BCF; husband of Nicole Wells-Stallworth
Nicole Wells-StallworthDaughter-in-lawMacDowell Board President; hired Brian Banks
Misha Stallworth WestGranddaughterDPSCD Board Member — authorizes MacDowell charter
Nicole StallworthDaughter-in-law (Keith’s wife)BCF Executive Director ($47,294 salary, 2015)

Legacy

Alma Stallworth’s 21-year legislative career represented genuine public service. This profile does not question that legacy.

But institutions outlive intentions. The BCF she founded became a vehicle for her son’s money laundering, a haven for convicted felons on its board, and the social network through which Brian Banks was connected to the family that would hire him to run a school.

The question is not whether Alma Stallworth intended this outcome. The question is why the institution she built was never held accountable when it became obvious what it had become.

All sources are public records.

The Hire ✅ Verified

Wells-Stallworth led the board that hired Brian Banks — a man with 9 criminal convictions including 6 felonies — as superintendent of MacDowell Preparatory Academy.

The Free Press (August 2023) asked why:

“Banks’ history of financial misdeeds is well-known to political insiders like Wells Stallworth and her fellow board members. In fact, Wells Stallworth said Banks’ troubled past is one of the reasons MacDowell’s board voted — unanimously — to hire him.”

She told the Free Press:

“It was determined by the board that he is well qualified, as an educator, a scholar, and a community leader.”

Left unanswered by the Free Press:

“whether Wells Stallworth is aware of Banks’ most recent financial problems and what role her family’s relationship with Banks played in the decision to hire him at MacDowell.”

The family’s relationship with Banks was forged at the Black Caucus Foundation of Michigan, where Banks served on the board alongside Keith Stallworth (Managing Director) and Thomas Stallworth III (Director).

The Campaign Donations

“The $1,250 that Wells Stallworth and her husband, Tommy, donated” made “them among Banks’ most generous supporters.”

— Detroit Free Press, Aug 27, 2023

The Cover-Up — 2 Hours, 24 Minutes ✅ Verified

On February 28, 2022, MDE sent a formal investigation letter to Wells-Stallworth regarding Banks operating without credentials. The MDE FOIA response (Sep 25, 2026) documented what happened next:

TimeEventActor
Feb 22, 12:24 PMMDE warns Banks has no credential — “the Academy is out of compliance with law”Leah Breen (MDE)
Feb 28, 8:26 AMInvestigation letter sent to Wells-StallworthKatie Schmiedeknecht (MDE)
Feb 28, ~8:40 AMWells-Stallworth loops in attorney — 14 minutesNicole Wells-Stallworth
Feb 28, 9:13 AMAttorney: “I have not fix for this at this time”Gregory Meihn (Foley & Mansfield)
Feb 28, 10:50 AMMDE: “no need for an investigation”Katie Schmiedeknecht (MDE)
Feb 28, 11:15 AMAttorney: “Thank you. Nicole, please call again”Gregory Meihn

Total elapsed: 2 hours, 24 minutes from investigation letter to clearance.

Wells-Stallworth retained a national law firm (Foley & Mansfield PLLP — offices in 13 cities) within 14 minutes of receiving the letter. An experienced public affairs executive with deep media and political connections deployed those connections to make a state investigation disappear in a single morning.
